name: The pantry
notes: The reference of fetch and serve; each dish's trip fetches its things (cook.json recipes.pantry.forDish). Zafar's 30 Oct notes call it weak (PAN-19 to 22).
proposal: L3: flour in the jar and flour in the bag, sugar in the tin and in the bottle: the container word decides. Positions and colours follow as planned.

name: Chai
notes: Signed off 7 Nov as the family's reference; the word moment (half, full) at L4.

name: Eggs at breakfast
notes: Lab prototype (1 Nov), not judged; tarelo and mari are drafts; boiled egg to record (R6-19).
proposal: Nana wants his fried, Ali wants his boiled: two eggs, a pan and a pot, and only the doing word says which. The count stays, but stops deciding.

name: Maani
notes: Live L1-L4; big and small at L4 in the she-forms.
proposal: Takes roll-tawa as its top level: two tawas, Nana's big ones on one and Ali's small ones on the other, so who and the size decide the tawa. L3 as today: Nana wants the big one, Nani the small one.

name: Roll-tawa
notes: Lab-only proof on maani's words; data/stations/roll-tawa.json names no words of its own. Thin: fold into maani's levels.
proposal: Becomes maani's top level (two tawas); it has no words of its own.

name: The corn stall
notes: Lab prototype on the grill kit (CK-67); a sekelo redress for the farm day; Nani stands in for Hannah Mami.
proposal: The beach stalls already hold the corn stall; one food-stall game, dressed for the farm or the beach.

name: Daar
notes: Live L1-L4; the vegetables and jeeru, rai are first met here (no earlier meeting).
proposal: L4: a little chilli for Ali's bowl, a lot for Nana's: the amount word sets the pinches.

name: Chop
notes: Its own game since Sprint 18; daar and chaat use it, so its words are theirs.
proposal: Three tools on the board. Nani says peel, grate or chop: the doing word picks the tool. Then 'small' or 'big pieces' sets how many swipes. The slicing stays exactly as it is.

name: Chaat
notes: Live L1-L4; 'no' asks from L2.
proposal: L3: Ali wants a lot of sev and a little chutney, the baby wants none: the amount word decides each layer.

name: Baking
notes: Lab prototype (1 Nov); the only game about how much; the amounts beyond half and full wait for Mum (R6-135).

name: Sekelo
notes: Live L1-L4; green pepper stays English until recorded.
proposal: L3: red and green pepper on the tray, same shape: 'red, then onion, then green'. The colour decides the pattern.

name: Samosa
notes: Live; SAM-35: the headline says the count.
proposal: L3: two fillings, 'Nana's without chilli, mine with': whose it is and 'without' decide the filling.

name: Clinic: the waiting room
notes: Describing-word ladder L1-L5; family words are a proposed rung (master map R7).
proposal: A new rung: patients come in their work clothes. Two men wait, a farmer and a postman: 'call the farmer'. The job word decides.

name: Clinic: diagnosis and where does it hurt?
notes: D1-D3 built; the body-chart prototype (2 Nov, where.js) widens it to 20+ parts; every named part must be treatable.

name: Clinic: the pharmacy belt
notes: Belt faster from L3, never a timer.

name: Clinic heal: scrape, knee, foot, boing, hand
notes: Numbers decide most live heal games (master map R7); the hand splinter is the 2 Nov prototype.
proposal: The tray always holds every tool. The doctor says 'clean it', 'wrap it' or 'pull it out': the doing word picks the tool. The counting stays as the second beat.

name: Clinic heal: ear, nose, eye, tooth
notes: The blocked nose is the 2 Nov prototype (the ear game's twin); the eye test's yes/no is the only speaking with real takes today.
proposal: Ear and nose are twins, so the body word must pick the game: the patient says which hurts and the close-up opens on what the child tapped.

name: Clinic heal: drinks and fever
notes: Fever keeps the doctor naming the effect to L3 (decision 91); drinks prototype 2 Nov.

name: Clinic: the send-off
notes: An apple, never a lolly; feelings are 'sad' or 'scared', always resolved gently (Zafar, 14 Oct).
proposal: The patient thanks 'the doctor' (the child) and 'the nurse' on the way out: jobs heard, nothing asked.

name: Clinic heal: tummy, hic, hair (parked)
notes: Parked per H32; their level 3 is level 2 heard only (decision 97).

name: Clinic: what's wrong?
notes: Suggested: the master map finds the health half of feelings short; the patient's 'why' line picks the cure.

name: Hide and seek
notes: Lab prototype (2 Nov); first of the day at home (places, then positions, then verbs).

name: Pick it up and put it back
notes: Lab prototype (2 Nov); two of the same thing in different places, so the place word decides.
proposal: Takes Tidy up's put-away rules as later levels; toys join the things carried between rooms.

name: Clean-up day
notes: Lab prototype (2 Nov); from L2 two of each, so on or off decides.
proposal: L3: a light is on in two rooms. 'Switch off the light in the kitchen': the room decides.

name: The wake-up clock
notes: Lab prototype (2 Nov); the only time game; from L2 the bedside clocks frost, so the heard hour decides.

name: Getting ready
notes: Lab prototype (2 Nov) on the do-it engine; jobs called in any order, so the verb decides, not the routine.
proposal: L3: Nani names two jobs, 'wash your face now, eat later'. The time word says which Ali does. At night the same game runs with pyjamas and bed.

name: Sewing: make
notes: Lab prototype (2 Nov); the rebuild of Dress up's Big Ma's sewing table.
proposal: Big Ma is 'the tailor' in Nani's lines: heard only.

name: Sewing: mend
notes: Lab prototype (2 Nov); always two faults, the said one decides.

name: Sewing: the fitting
notes: Lab prototype (2 Nov); Dress up's 'the fitting' rebuilt.

name: The door

grammar.pattern: Want to, have to, can, can't

notes: A beat, not a test, today: the weather words are in data/day.json but decide nothing. Suggested: Nani says the sky before the curtain opens and the child picks its card, so the weather word decides.

name: The evening book
notes: Reviews whatever the day log holds; the only place with past forms (we saw, we went).
proposal: Takes 'the day in order' as a page: two or three of today's photos, 'first... then... after'. The time word decides the order.

name: Conversations

grammar.pattern: Want to, have to, can, can't

notes: Engine and lab live, not yet wired into pages; woven round every mode.

name: First launch

grammar.pattern: Want to, have to, can, can't

notes: Its hook still says Eid; to be reworded for the birthday (Zafar, 31 Oct).

name: What's missing?
notes: Suggested: the mind verbs (know, remember, find) have no game; answered by voice (research-mechanics), so no tap-matching leak.

name: Tell Ali which one
notes: Suggested: no game where the describing word is the move (master map Part 6); 'behind the screen' from Table 1, speaking in a closed set of 2-3.

name: The day in order
notes: Suggested as an evening-book page: time words (now, later, before, after) are short in every map.
proposal: A page of the evening book, not a game of its own.

name: Ali's play room
notes: Suggested: the clean-up's planned later visit (Ali's room) made a game; toys have no primary home, and push and hold are missing top-40 verbs.

name: Find it (the errand)
notes: Built on its own engine (25 Sept), next onto the shared core; the shops use it.
proposal: Sizes stop deciding here (picky shopping owns them); the errand stays food and count.

name: Pack the bag
notes: A reskin of the pantry fetch; the weather sets the kind, the Kutchi picks which and how many.
proposal: Nani says only the weather ('it's raining today') or only the game ('Ali has cricket'): the child packs what that needs. One trip, one kind of bag, so the nine groups never arrive together.

name: The window ride
notes: Built (Sprint 9); the farm road is data; the sea, jeep and boat roads reuse it.
proposal: On the town road people pass as well as things: 'the postman', on a bike beside two other riders.

name: Put it in its place
notes: An engine: its nouns come from each stage (feed, animals home, the picnic, the shopping).
proposal: An engine, not a game the child sees: its words are its stages' (the picnic, home at dusk, the watering hole).

name: Count to a heard number
notes: An engine (Cook's count generalised); eggs, cobs, shells, coins.
proposal: An engine, not a game the child sees: its words are its stages' (the orchard, the eggs, the cake, Pay).

name: Meet the host
notes: The Meet stage of every trip (farm, beach, safari) on Conversations; the child answers with the elder form.
proposal: Nani introduces the host by their work: heard only.

name: Pass the balloon
notes: Party lab prototype (2 Nov); from L2 the two sisters swap seats, so mum or aunt decides.
proposal: L3: two balloons in the air. 'The red one to Masi, the blue one to Mum': colour and family word decide together.

name: How are you?
notes: Party prototype (2 Nov); all six fixes always there, so the feeling word picks.

name: Musical statues
notes: Party prototype (2 Nov) on the do-it engine; the only home for moving-yourself verbs.
proposal: L3: Nana drums and Masi sings. 'Dance to the drum, sit for the song': the music word decides. No one is ever out.

name: The cake
notes: Party prototype (2 Nov) on word tiles; the birthday stays though celebrations are out.

name: The party presents
notes: Party prototype (2 Nov); any toy can go to anyone, so the owner decides.
proposal: L1-L2: two presents are for Zara, the doll and the ball: the toy word decides. From L3 the owner decides, as today.

name: Snap the guests
notes: Comes later; Snap's engine is a rebuild (master map G).

name: Who ate the cake?
notes: Second party visit, on Who did it?'s engine; the clue must be heard, not seen.

name: Pack the school bag
notes: School day lab prototype (2 Nov); later how many and whose decide.
proposal: The twist level: 'it's games day', so today the ball does go in. The decoy becomes the answer.

name: The blackboard
notes: School day prototype (2 Nov); no letters or numbers on the board; shapes wait on Mum.
proposal: The teacher names the tool before the drawing: 'take the crayon', 'rub it out with the duster'. The school word decides what is in the hand.

name: The town map

grammar.pattern: Want to, have to, can, can't

notes: Town prototype (2 Nov); Zafar's harder level says 'I want a book', not 'the library'.
proposal: Zafar's inference level, with people: 'I need the doctor', 'Nana wants the tailor', 'Ali wants to play cricket'. The job or the game picks the place.

name: Serve at the fruit stall
notes: Town prototype (2 Nov); the child serves, later orders.
proposal: Each sale ends with Pay: the customer asks 'how much?', and the heard price is counted in. Pay becomes the stalls' last scene, not a game alone.

name: Nani's picky shopping
notes: Town prototype (2 Nov); two of the same side by side.
proposal: L2: a big pot beside a big pan: the thing decides. L3: 'not the old one, the new one'. Nani's 'too dear!' is the running gag.

name: Pay
notes: Town prototype (2 Nov); coins carry no digits; to 20, then 100 as levels rise (Zafar, 1 Nov).
proposal: Stays as built, but plays as the closing scene of the fruit, cloth and beach stalls.

name: The lanes
notes: Zafar's first-person maze (19 Oct); 'this side, that side' before left and right (Mum, idea 11).
proposal: Nani names where to go, not just the turns: two shop fronts at a fork, 'to the bakery'. The place word decides.

name: The goat chase
notes: Designed for the shops day; people along the lanes say which way it went.
proposal: Two people stand at each corner. 'Ask the shopkeeper': the job says whose pointing to follow.

name: Big Ma's cloth stall
notes: Sewing prototype (2 Nov); also the shops' third trip; seeds the sewing day.
proposal: 'Cloth for a scarf' or 'cloth for a kurta': the garment word picks the length Big Ma cuts.

name: Feeding time
notes: Farm prototype (1 Nov); hens and goats both want food, so the word picks.
proposal: The goat wants more, the hen has had enough: the amount word says who gets the next scoop.

name: Collect the eggs
notes: Farm prototype (1 Nov); peeking under any hen is free.
proposal: Colour stops deciding; number and size are enough here.

name: The farm photo shoot
notes: Farm prototype (data/farm/photo.json); its photos feed the evening book.
proposal: Its own USP made true: three goats, one eating, one running, one asleep. Only the doing word picks the shot.

name: Home at dusk
notes: Farm prototype (1 Nov); planned later: call the animal over (speaking).

name: Pick (the orchard)
notes: Farm prototype, second visit; more on the tree than asked.
proposal: 'From the tall tree', 'the ones on the ground', 'not the flowers': the plant word says where the fruit comes from.

name: Plant and water
notes: Farm prototype, second visit; the only plants game.
proposal: Before going out Nani says 'it rained in the night' or 'the sun has been out': water the beds, or don't. The weather word decides.

name: Pet hotel: look after the animals
notes: Pets prototype (2 Nov); Hannah Mami's centre, 'not a vet' (Zafar).

name: Pet hotel: going home
notes: Pets prototype (2 Nov); one line, same size, all happy, so only the name picks.
proposal: The owners come to collect: 'the rabbit goes home with the teacher'. Pet and owner both decide. The postman's pet is the gag.

name: Snap from the jeep
notes: Safari prototype (2 Nov); three of a kind doing different things from L2.

name: Who's hiding?
notes: Safari prototype (2 Nov); body and describing words on animals.

name: The watering hole
notes: In the safari's first sketch (find-it or put-it-in-its-place); not designed further.

name: Shells
notes: Beach prototype (2 Nov); needs Mum's beach words.

name: The sandcastle
notes: Beach prototype (2 Nov); the tower's height shows the amount.

name: The beach stalls
notes: Beach prototype (2 Nov); Cook reskins (corn, cassava chips, coconut).
proposal: Takes the corn stall. The child is the stall-keeper: 'with lemon, without chilli' dresses the corn, then 'how much?' and Pay.

name: The picnic
notes: Beach prototype (2 Nov); every spot outlined, never just the right one.

name: The kite
notes: Only if it earns its place as a game (Zafar, 19 Oct).
proposal: The kite becomes one of the park's things (hold, let go), so it earns its place inside a game.

name: The ride on the water
notes: Boat-day prototype (2 Nov) on the window ride.

name: Litter fishing
notes: Boat-day prototype (2 Nov); weak as its own game (research), so one stage of the boat day.
proposal: 'Catch the tin, leave the crab': litter or sea creature decides. Stays one stage of the boat day.

name: Tidy up
notes: Greybox; to fold into pick it up and the clean-up (Zafar, 31 Oct: yes, after the list of which go where).
merged_into: Pick it up and put it back
proposal: Zafar, 31 Oct: fold in. Its put-away rules become later levels.

name: Dress up
notes: Greybox; the sewing prototypes are its rebuild.
proposal: The fitting is its rebuild.

name: Who did it?
notes: Greybox; 'who did it?' (kere karein) is not confirmed: don't use (conversations §4).
proposal: The same game; the party version is the one planned.

name: Monsoon rush
notes: Greybox; the proposed monsoon day.

name: Snap
notes: Greybox (the still orchard); its engine returns at the farm, the party and the safari.
proposal: The greybox is retired; the camera returns at the farm, the safari and the party.

name: The park

grammar.pattern: Want to, have to, can, can't

notes: Suggested: a stage of the town day on the do-it engine, in the park already on the town map. It gives sports their one home, takes the kite, and brings back kick, throw and catch. Not a sports day (Zafar, 31 Oct): no scores, no losers.
proposal: 'Let's play cricket': a football, a cricket ball and a bat lie on the grass, and the game word picks the kit. Then Nana calls 'throw', 'hit', 'catch'. When the wind comes: 'hold the kite... let go'.
